metadata.title: Planar Keller Maps after the Counterexample: Weight-Class Exclusions, a Chart Atlas, and a Conditional Exclusion of the Degree Pair (72,108) by Independent Proofs of Cases 1 and 2
metadata.description:
The July 2026 counterexample settled the Jacobian conjecture in every dimension N ≥ 3 and left the planar case JC(2) open. This paper studies the planar case in exact arithmetic. Four exclusion theorems follow from a weight-class calculus: a two-term P = x + a x^u y^v is never a Keller component, nor is any lower-weight perturbation of it; no component has a Newton top edge anchored at the linear vertex x with interior direction; and if x is a vertex of the Newton polygon then P = x + f(y). A fifth exclusion, the transport of the Keller constant along the staircase that swallows x, is proved at every partner degree for six certified grid shapes. The single degree pair (72,108) left open below 125 by Guccione, Guccione, Horruitiner and Valqui reduces to two coefficient systems, Cases 1 and 2. We prove Case 2 empty by a standard basis, and Case 1 empty by single-prime resultant-chain certificates with proven degree bounds: a three-leaf tree of Rabinowitsch splits on each of two branches, checked at a second prime, in Singular and at third primes, where exact standard bases and multi-modular certificates had not finished. A chart atlas closes four-coefficient sub-families of Case 1. Conditionally on their Proposition 4.3 being exhaustive and on our encoding of its polygons, no Keller pair has degrees (72,108) or (108,72), so by their Theorem 2.1, whose (9,24) step we check against the hypotheses of their Theorem 5.1 (EXP-147), a counterexample has maximal degree at least 125; priority is Helali's. JC(2) remains open.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/algebraic-geometry/jacobian-conjecture).
metadata.version_notes: A resultant-chain certificate that Case 1 of the (72,108) reduction is empty is added: a new algorithm (single-prime chains with proven degree bounds, Rabinowitsch splits and exact division), its correctness proof, the trees of both branches, the gates and the checks at a second prime, in Singular and at third primes. With the Case 2 result this excludes the degree pairs (72,108) and (108,72) conditionally on Proposition 4.3 of Guccione, Guccione, Horruitiner and Valqui being exhaustive and on the encoding of its polygons, so that by their Theorem 2.1, whose (9,24) step is checked here against the hypotheses of their Theorem 5.1 (EXP-147), a counterexample has maximal degree at least 125; priority for the exclusion is Helali's. The title, abstract, introduction, related work, methods (a seventh procedure and its software), experimental design, frontier section, the scope statements of the Proposition 4.3 and atlas sections, ablation, discussion, limitations, open problems, conclusions and data availability are rewritten accordingly; the cost, ablation, notation and reproducibility tables gain the certificate's rows, and the frontier ladder gains the conditional floor row.
